hlaunit.hla13.common

Class Test13Federate

  • java.lang.Object
    • hlaunit.hla13.common.Test13Federate

  • public class Test13Federate
extends Object
    This class represents a federate that can be used for testing purposes. It provides a number of helper methods that speed the process of writing tests

      • quickResign

        public void quickResign(int resignAction)
        Centralize the resign processing just to make things easier. If there is a problem while attempting the resign, this method will use Assert.fail() to fail the test rather than throw an exception. If the federate is not currently joined (and a FederateNotExecutionMember exception is thrown), it will be ignored.

      • quickSaveInProgress

        public void quickSaveInProgress(String label)
        This method will trigger a save request with the given label and then wait until a callback initiating the save have been received. If there is a problem sending out the request or the initiation isn't received in a timely fashion, the current test will be failed.

        The main purpose of this method is for getting a federation to a point where the "SaveInProgress" exceptions can be tested for.

      • quickSaveToCompletion

        public void quickSaveToCompletion(String label)
        This method will handle the entire save process, triggering and completing the process using the given label. A reference to each of the federates is taken from the test to which this federate is attached. Note that this method will call methods on the other federates as required to complete the save.

        At the end of this process, the federation will have been successfully saved using the given label. If there is a problem in any of the steps (initiating the save, starting it or successfully completing in any of the federates), the current test will be failed.

      • quickRestoreRequest

        public void quickRestoreRequest(String label)
        Requests a federation restore from the RTIambassador and then returns. If there is an exception performing this call, the current test is failed.

      • quickRestoreRequestSuccess

        public void quickRestoreRequestSuccess(String label)
        This method initiates a federation restore request (calling quickRestoreRequest(String)) and then ticks until either a success of failure notification from the RTI is received. If the initiation is not a success, or there is an exception initiating it, the current test is failed.

        **NOTE** This will block until a notification from the RTI is received about whether the request was a failure or a success. If you just want to initiate a restore, use the quickRestoreRequest(String) method.

        Parameters:
        label -

      • quickRestoreComplete

      • quickRestoreNotComplete

        Tell the RTIambassador that the federate has *NOT* successfully completed it's restore. If there is an exception, the current test is failed.

      • quickRestoreInProgress

        public void quickRestoreInProgress(String label)
        This method will trigger and complete a Save and then initiate a restore, waiting for a callback indicating that the federation restore has begun. The given label is used both for the save and the restore. The set of all the federates is received from the test class that this federate is associated with.

        The main purpose of this method is for getting a federation to a point where the "RestoreInProgress" exceptions can be tested for.

      • quickRestoreToCompletion

        This method is much like quickSaveToCompletion(String), except for restoration. It runs through the complete restore cycle, making sure all the federates get the right messages and respond appropriately. This is primarily intended for use in methods which test that some state that was present before a save is properly set after a restore.

        NOTE: For this method to work properly you will need to have previously completed a federation save with the same label given as a parameter

      • quickExchangeOwnership

        public void quickExchangeOwnership(Test13Federate owningFederate,
                                   int theObject,
                                   int... attributes)
        Exchange ownership between the current federate (requesting) and the given owner federate. Exchange requires action by both federates, so this method will trigger each of the current and owning federates to behave appropriately at the right times.

        The exchange process:

        1. (This federate) Requests ownership acquisition
        2. (Owning federate) Wait for ownership request
        3. (Owning federate) Releases ownership through release response
        4. (This federate) Waits until it has received ownership

        public void quickEnableConstrained()
        Turns on time constrained and blocks until either the callback is received or a timeout occurs. If there is a timeout, Assert.fail is used to kill the test.

      • quickAdvanceFederation

        public void quickAdvanceFederation(double newTime)
        This method will advance all federates associated with the same test as this federate to the given time. This is just a helper method to handle the advancement process when multiple federates are involved. Doing this with pure requests/waitFor's requires a couple of extra steps (for example, you can only advanceAndWait() in the last regulating federate because if you do this on a constrained federate it might not give a regulating federate a chance to advance, thus causing the wait to fail - and other such circumstances).

        The method will get access to all the joined federates from the Abstract13Test and will invoke requests on them, before invoking advances on them later when it should be safe.

        Parameters:
        newTime -

        public void quickTickSingle(double wait)
